newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria, German BASF plan Spanish petchem plant.
newsitem.headline: Algeria, German BASF plan Spanish petchem plant.

text.p: Algeria's state-owned gas and oil firm Sonatrach and the German BASF AG group signed a letter of intent to set a 350,000 tonnes propylene output joint-venture in Spain, Sonatrach said on Saturday.

"Sonatrach and BASF have started following the signing (of the letter of intent) a feasibility study which sould end on a finale decision at the beginning of next year (1998)," said the Algerian firm in a statement.

The joint-venture, with a processing capacity of 450,000 tonnes of gas propane into 350,000 tonnes of propylene, will be built in Terragone, in Spain, the seat of BASF affiliate, Targor, the statement said.
Under the letter of intent terms, Sonatrach will supply the unit with 450,000 tonnes of propane from the Algerian Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) plant in Bethioua, said the statement.
Algeria began on December 1996 expanding an LPG gas complex at Bethioua, at the coast of the western province of Oran, to lift capacity by 2.2 million tonnes to seven million tonnes a year.
The upgrading work should be finished in 28 months bringing Algeria to the rank of second world producer and exporter of LPG.
Sonatrach said on Saturday the initial accord with BASF was a prelude to more co-operation between the two firms in other downstream petrochemical projects in Algeria.
It gave no more figures on the planned joint-venture but it said BASF'S subsidiary Targor Gmbh will buy all its propylene output.
